title: Anguila Peluda: The Hairy Eel Legend of Anaga, Tenerife
metaDescription: The Anguila peluda, or hairy eel, belongs to stories about Anaga in Tenerife. A nineteenth-century expedition account connects the legend to a real pool and ravine.
description: The Anguila peluda, or hairy eel, belongs to stories about Anaga in Tenerife. A nineteenth-century expedition account connects the legend to a real pool and ravine.
storyHooks: A guide and a visitor reach the legendary pool. One wants to publish its location; the other fears what an audience will change.

sections.origin: Anguila peluda means hairy eel. This entry concerns Anaga, in northeastern Tenerife, rather than a creature said to inhabit every part of Spain.
sections.legend: Andrés Raya Ramos reproduces a passage from Manuel de Ossuna’s Anaga y sus antigüedades (1897), describing an expedition in August 1889. The travellers approach a pool associated with the feared eel. The narrative describes terrain and apprehension; it does not report the capture of such an animal.
sections.variants: Raya Ramos also notes the place-name Charco de la Anguila on modern mapping. A surviving place-name helps locate a story, but does not establish the existence or anatomy of its monster.
sections.culture: A Canary Islands school’s account of the 2023 Los Silos storytelling festival includes the eel of Anaga among the legends presented to pupils. The story continues to circulate through local storytelling.

researchNote: The historical passage was read through a modern transcription, not checked against a scan of the 1897 edition.

questions.question: Where is this legend set?
questions.answer: In Anaga on Tenerife, in the Canary Islands.

questions.question: Did Ossuna find a hairy eel?
questions.answer: The transcribed passage describes the expedition and pool, not a captured or verified monster.
